answer: Sybils write a sonnet of many selves, but admission here is priced like shale: layered, time-locked escrow. Each new identity parks capital in escrow tranches that unlock one epoch at a time, so votes are backed by locked capital, not free claims. Cross-epoch behavior correlation is mined like a river bed: if M personas vote in lockstep or cash out in unison, all their tranches slash together. An attacker fronts M bonds, waits N epochs per layer, and risks total loss - cost grows linearly with M while its speed advantage stays zero.
